quiz.title: Tangents and Normals Quiz (Exercise 6.3)
quiz.intro: Eight questions on slopes, tangent lines and normal lines drawn from NCERT Exercise 6.3. Choose an answer for each, then press Check my score.
quiz.about: NCERT Class 12 Application of Derivatives Exercise 6.3 — tangents and normals

questions.q: The slope of the tangent to a curve y = f(x) at a point is given by which quantity?
options: The value of y at that point
questions.explanation: The slope of the tangent to y = f(x) at any point equals the derivative dy/dx evaluated at that point.

questions.q: Find the slope of the tangent to y = x² at the point (2, 4).
questions.explanation: dy/dx = 2x, so at x = 2 the slope is 2(2) = 4.

questions.q: The slope of the normal to a curve at a point where the tangent slope is m (m ≠ 0) is:
questions.explanation: The normal is perpendicular to the tangent, so its slope is the negative reciprocal, −1/m.

questions.q: At which points is the tangent to y = x² − 4x + 3 parallel to the x-axis?
questions.explanation: A horizontal tangent needs dy/dx = 0. Here 2x − 4 = 0 gives x = 2.

questions.q: The equation of the tangent to y = x² at (1, 1) is:
questions.explanation: Slope = 2x = 2 at x = 1. Using y − 1 = 2(x − 1) gives y = 2x − 1.

questions.q: A tangent is vertical (parallel to the y-axis) when:
questions.explanation: A vertical tangent occurs where the slope dy/dx is undefined, i.e. where dx/dy = 0.

questions.q: The slope of the normal to y = x³ at the point (1, 1) is:
questions.explanation: dy/dx = 3x² = 3 at x = 1, so the tangent slope is 3 and the normal slope is −1/3.

questions.q: The equation of the normal to y = x² at (1, 1), where the tangent slope is 2, is:
questions.explanation: Normal slope = −1/2. Using y − 1 = −½(x − 1) gives x + 2y = 3.

faq.q: How do you find the slope of a tangent in Exercise 6.3?
faq.a: Differentiate the curve to get dy/dx, then substitute the point's coordinates. The value of dy/dx at that point is the slope of the tangent there.

faq.q: How is the slope of the normal related to the slope of the tangent?
faq.a: The normal is perpendicular to the tangent, so its slope is the negative reciprocal. If the tangent slope is m, the normal slope is −1/m, provided m is not zero.

faq.q: What does a horizontal or vertical tangent mean?
faq.a: A tangent is horizontal (parallel to the x-axis) where dy/dx = 0. It is vertical (parallel to the y-axis) where dy/dx is undefined, which is where dx/dy = 0.

faq.q: How do you write the equation of a tangent or a normal line?
faq.a: Find the slope at the given point, then use the point-slope form y − y₁ = m(x − x₁). Use the tangent slope for the tangent line and the negative-reciprocal slope for the normal line.
